interactions_implemented: per-boid steering-force vector overlay toggle (amber arrows)
live polarization R readout + regime label

model.rules: Reynolds separation + alignment + cohesion (no predator, no leader)
model.integration: one fixed Euler step per frame; velocity clamped to max_speed
model.polarization: magnitude of mean unit-velocity vector (Kuramoto order-parameter analog)

gotchas_hit: d3-force is a relaxation solver, not a kinematic integrator: to reproduce the Reynolds max-speed Euler step exactly we set velocityDecay(0), alphaDecay(0), alphaMin(0) and the custom force REPLACES velocity rather than accumulating into it. The naive add-to-vx-with-default-decay approach cools toward zero and will not match the p5/Plot trajectory.

Snapshot correctness: the Reynolds step must read all old positions/velocities before writing any new velocity. Three separate accumulating d3 forces (sep/align/cohesion) would let alignment read velocities already mutated by separation within the same tick, breaking the honest-comparison discipline. Implemented as ONE two-pass force.
d3-force reserves node.fx / node.fy for FIXED positions. Naming a steering-force field fx/fy silently pins every boid in place. Used steerX/steerY instead.
Toroidal wrap done in the tick handler after d3-force's x += vx; the minimum-image delta is computed inside the neighbor search, not only on position update.

verification.method: static server + headless eval/screenshot; d3.timerFlush() pumped (rAF paused in harness)

notes: Determinism cross-checked in Node against the identical shared model block (bit-identical trajectories across runs; speed cap honored at 3.0000). Trajectory provably identical to the Plot and p5 Specimens (same seed, same shared computeVelocities). Sketch tier: no mobile, no ARIA, no keyboard nav.
